description: Change a campaign's settings: send only what changes. `schedule` names every weekday (`mon` to `sun`), each with up to 4 sending windows as `HH:MM` in the workspace's time zone. An empty list is a day off, and at least one day needs a window. `dailyLimit` is emails a day across all its mailboxes, 1 to 20,000. `unsubscribeMode`: `link` adds an unsubscribe link under each email, `text` asks the reader to reply if they want to stop, `off` adds nothing. `stopOnReply`: a person's reply ends that lead's sequence. `textOnly`: send plain text with no HTML part. `trackOpens`: put an invisible image in each HTML email to record when it is opened. `trackClicks`: send the links written in each step's HTML through the tracking domain to record the click; the reader lands on the same page. Links in the mailbox's signature, the unsubscribe link, links that aren't http or https (mailto:, tel:), every link past the first 100 in an email, and every link in the plain-text part go out as written. Turning either on needs one of the workspace's tracking domains verified (list_tracking_domains); emails carry the image and tracked links only while one is `inUse`, and go out without them meanwhile. Both are off by default because on cold email they can send more mail to spam. `sendToRisky` and `sendToUnknown` let a first email go to an address whose fresh check said `risky` or couldn't tell (`unknown`); both start off, and those leads wait in review. Turning one on adds to whom it writes; turning one off does not. Pacing: `rampStart` starts the day's limit low (`null` turns the ramp off) and it climbs by `rampIncrement` after each day it sent, up to `dailyLimit`; `maxNewLeadsPerDay` caps the leads that get their first email in a day (`null`: no cap), and follow-ups never count; `entryDelayMinutes` makes a lead wait after it is added, up to 129,600 minutes (90 days); `newLeadsFirst` sends first emails before follow-ups (off: follow-ups first); `continuous` keeps it running when every lead is done, waiting for leads you add (off: it finishes). A one-time campaign never waits: continuous: true on one answers 409 oneTimeNotContinuous. A slower pace, a later start, the order and `continuous` only take something out; a faster pace adds. `cc` and `bcc`: up to 5 addresses each that every email of the campaign also goes to, such as a colleague or your CRM. The lead sees Cc and never Bcc. An email leaves out the lead's own address, and any address on the suppression list or known to be invalid (list_campaign_log says so). Copies count toward no daily limit here, but your email provider counts each one as another recipient. A reply from a copy never counts as the lead's. A new address, or one moved between Cc and Bcc, adds to whom it writes; taking one out doesn't. Test emails go to you only. On a running campaign, a change that adds to what it sends or to whom also needs the `send` permission, and makes the caller its approver. Through an API key an owner limited, the key's limits must cover the campaign, every mailbox it sends from and outreach, or it answers 403 with `details.scope` naming the limit. A change that only takes something out needs none of that.

bcc.description: Addresses every step also goes to without the lead seeing them: up to 5, [] for none. An address in both lists stays in cc. A bcc address with letters outside a to z before the @ goes only to an email whose mail server offers SMTPUTF8; otherwise it is left out of that email and the campaign's history says so. Otherwise as cc.

cc.description: Addresses every step also goes to, in the Cc line the lead sees: up to 5, [] for none. Each email leaves out any that is on the suppression list or was found invalid. Only the letters a to z, digits and symbols are allowed before the @, because the Cc line is written before the mail server is known: put any other address in bcc. A reply from one of them lands in the inbox as ordinary mail and never stops, holds or suppresses the lead. Your mail provider counts each one as another recipient toward its own daily limit; the campaign's limits count the email once. Adding an address to a running campaign needs the send permission, and you become its approver.

continuous.description: Keep running when every lead's sequence has ended, and write to leads added later. Off: the campaign finishes.

entryDelayMinutes.description: How long a lead waits after it is added before its first email.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

maxNewLeadsPerDay.description: The most leads that get their first email in one day, on the workspace's clock. Follow-ups never count. null: no limit.

newLeadsFirst.description: First emails go before follow-ups. Off by default: follow-ups go first.

rampIncrement.description: How much the ramp's limit climbs after each day it sent.

rampStart.description: Start low: the first day's limit. The limit then climbs by rampIncrement after each day it sent, up to dailyLimit. null turns the ramp off; turning it on again starts over.

trackClicks.description: Send the links written in each step's HTML through one of the workspace's tracking domains, which records the click and takes the reader on to the same page. Links in the mailbox's signature, the unsubscribe link, links that aren't http or https (mailto:, tel:) and every link past the first 100 in an email go out as written. Turning it on needs a verified tracking domain (list_tracking_domains); emails carry tracked links only while one is inUse. Off by default: on cold email it can send more mail to spam.

trackOpens.description: Put an invisible image in each HTML email to record when it is opened. Turning it on needs a verified tracking domain (list_tracking_domains); emails carry the image only while one is inUse. Off by default: on cold email it can send more mail to spam.
